name: Comps Set Builder

inputs.name: Purpose: valuation, pitch, fairness context or interview answer
Any house view on must-include / must-exclude names

steps.title: Define comparability
steps.detail: Business model, end markets, growth, margins, scale, geography — write the criteria BEFORE listing names.

steps.title: Build the long list
steps.detail: Cast wide: direct competitors, adjacent models, the names every banker includes by convention.

steps.title: Screen to a short list
steps.detail: Apply the criteria explicitly. Every exclusion gets a one-line reason — that’s what makes the set defensible.

steps.title: Sanity-check the spread
steps.detail: If the multiples range is enormous, the set is probably mixing business models. Segment or trim.

steps.title: Document the rationale
steps.detail: One table: name, why included, key differences, flags (low float, distressed, pending deal).

steps.title: Delegate 1
steps.detail: Generating the candidate long list from industry classifications and filings

steps.title: Delegate 2
steps.detail: Pulling descriptive stats (size, growth, margins) for screening

sections.name: Comps
sections.detail: Market, capital structure, operating metrics, trailing and forward multiples, median and mean — every multiple a live formula

sections.name: Inclusion
sections.detail: Why each name is in, which names were rejected and why, and every adjustment made. An empty rejection list is flagged in the sheet as a red flag.

sections.name: Sources
sections.detail: Every filing-derived figure resolved to tag, period, form and accession

outputs.sourcePolicy: Fundamentals from each filer’s XBRL tags. Share price and forward consensus are shaded input cells for your own licensed feed — the workbook will not guess a price and then print a multiple off it. EBITDA is built from operating income plus D&A in the sheet, because EBITDA is not a GAAP tag.

verification.description: Candidates actually do what the classification says they do
No pending-takeover or distressed names polluting trading multiples unflagged
Financial metrics used for screening are calendarised and like-for-like
Every exclusion has a written reason
Set size is 5-10 names or explicitly segmented
You can defend the set out loud in 60 seconds

humanCheckpoints: The comparability criteria themselves — that’s the analytical judgment
Whether to segment the set (e.g. high-growth vs mature) rather than force one universe

display.jobToBeDone: Choose a defensible comparable-companies universe, and be able to defend every inclusion.
